learn.hook: Cross two pencils and look closely — you have just made four angles with a secret pattern!
points: Two lines that meet at a point are called intersecting lines. They make 4 angles at that point.
Angles opposite each other across the meeting point are vertically opposite angles. They are always equal.
Two angles next to each other on a straight line form a linear pair. They add up to 180°.
All four angles around the meeting point add up to 360°.
If one of the four angles is 90°, all four are 90°, and the lines are perpendicular.

example.q: Two lines intersect. One of the angles is 65°. Find the other three angles.
steps: The angle next to 65° on the straight line is 180° − 65° = 115°
The angle opposite 65° is also 65° (vertically opposite)

learn.reallife: Scissor blades, a road crossing and the letter X all show intersecting lines and vertically opposite angles.

items.text: Angles on a straight line add up to ___°
The four angles where two lines cross add up to ___°
If one angle where two lines cross is 90°, the lines are ___
If one angle is 40°, its partner on the straight line is ___°

quiz.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 65°. What is the angle vertically opposite to it?
quiz.explain: Vertically opposite angles are always equal, so it is 65°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the opposite angle and the given angle add up to 180°

quiz.q: Two lines cross. One angle is 65°. What is the angle next to it on the same straight line?
quiz.explain: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 65° = 115°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 90° instead of 180°

quiz.q: Two lines intersect and one of the angles is 90°. What are the other three angles?
quiz.explain: The neighbour is 180° − 90° = 90°, and opposite angles are equal. So all four are right angles.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only one angle can be a right angle

quiz.q: Two angles form a linear pair and are equal to each other. What is each angle?
quiz.explain: A linear pair adds up to 180°. Two equal parts: 180° ÷ 2 = 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each angle of a linear pair is 180°

quiz.q: Three of the four angles where two lines cross are 110°, 70° and 110°. What is the fourth angle?
quiz.explain: All four add to 360°. 360° − (110° + 70° + 110°) = 360° − 290° = 70°. It is also opposite the other 70°.
quiz.mistake: Adds the three angles and forgets to subtract from 360°

quiz.q: Which pair of angles could form a linear pair?
quiz.explain: A linear pair must add up to 180°. Only 100° + 80° = 180°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a linear pair adds up to 90° or that the angles must be equal

quiz.q: Lines AB and CD intersect at O. ∠AOC = 40°. What is ∠AOD?
quiz.explain: ∠AOC and ∠AOD sit side by side on the straight line CD, so they add to 180°. 180° − 40° = 140°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks ∠AOD is vertically opposite to ∠AOC

quiz.q: Which of these is the best example of perpendicular lines?
options: Two edges at the corner of a notebook
The two strokes of the letter V
quiz.explain: The corner of a notebook is a right angle (90°), so its edges are perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two meeting lines are perpendicular

teach.ask: Gappu crossed two sticks and saw four angles. How are these angles connected? Explain!
teach.praise: Wow! Opposite angles are twins and neighbours make 180°. Gappu is amazed!
teach.nudge: What do two neighbouring angles on a straight line add up to?

topics.title: Naming angles and marking right angles

learn.hook: Can two straight roads cross each other twice? Try drawing it — you'll find it is impossible!
points: Two different straight lines can meet at most at one point.
If lines AB and CD meet at O, the four angles are ∠AOC, ∠COB, ∠BOD and ∠DOA.
Linear pairs sit side by side on a straight line: ∠AOC and ∠COB, ∠COB and ∠BOD, ∠BOD and ∠DOA, ∠DOA and ∠AOC.
Vertically opposite pairs face each other: ∠AOC and ∠BOD, ∠COB and ∠DOA.
A small square at a corner marks a right angle. AB ⊥ CD means AB is perpendicular to CD.

example.q: Lines AB and CD meet at O and ∠AOC = 50°. Find ∠BOD, ∠COB and ∠AOD.

learn.reallife: Road signs for a crossroad, and the corner of a door frame marked with a little square on building plans, use these ideas.

games.title: Lines AB and CD cross at O

∠AOC and ∠BOD
∠COB and ∠DOA

games.title: Lines and marks
items: Two different straight lines can cross at two points
Straight lines can share at most one point.
A small square drawn at a corner means 90°
That is the right-angle mark.
AB ⊥ CD means AB is parallel to CD
⊥ means perpendicular; ∥ means parallel.
Two crossing lines make 2 pairs of vertically opposite angles
∠AOC & ∠BOD, and ∠COB & ∠DOA.
Two crossing lines make 4 linear pairs
Each neighbouring pair of angles is a linear pair.

quiz.q: At most how many points can two different straight lines have in common?
quiz.explain: If they shared two points they would be the same line, so different lines share at most one point.
quiz.mistake: Thinks lines can bend back and cross again

quiz.q: Lines AB and CD meet at O. Which angle is vertically opposite to ∠AOC?
quiz.explain: OA and OB are opposite rays, and so are OC and OD. So ∠AOC faces ∠BOD.
quiz.mistake: Picks an angle next to it instead of across from it

quiz.q: Lines AB and CD meet at O. Which pair is a linear pair?
quiz.explain: ∠AOC and ∠COB share the arm OC and together make the straight angle AOB.
quiz.mistake: Confuses vertically opposite angles with a linear pair

quiz.q: Lines AB and CD meet at O and ∠AOC = 50°. What is ∠COB?
quiz.explain: ∠AOC and ∠COB form a linear pair: 180° − 50° = 130°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the neighbouring angle is equal

quiz.q: Lines AB and CD meet at O. If ∠BOC = 112°, what is ∠AOD?
quiz.explain: ∠BOC and ∠AOD are vertically opposite, so they are equal.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180° even though the angles are vertically opposite

quiz.q: How many linear pairs are formed when two lines intersect?
quiz.explain: Going round the point, each angle and the next one form a linear pair: 4 pairs.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the vertically opposite pairs

quiz.q: What does a small square drawn at the corner where two lines meet tell you?
options: The lines are the same length
quiz.explain: The small square is the standard mark for a right angle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the square is just decoration

quiz.q: Which symbol means 'is perpendicular to'?
quiz.explain: ⊥ looks like a line standing straight on another; ∥ means parallel.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parallel and perpendicular symbols

teach.ask: Gappu drew two lines AB and CD crossing at O. Which angles are partners, and why?
teach.praise: Wonderful! Gappu can name every angle at a crossing.
teach.nudge: Which angles face each other, and which sit side by side on a straight line?

learn.hook: Railway tracks run side by side for hundreds of kilometres and never bump into each other. How?
points: Parallel lines are lines on a flat surface that never meet, however far you extend them. We write l ∥ m.
Parallel lines stay the same distance apart everywhere.
Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle (90°). We write l ⊥ m.
On a flat page, two different lines either meet (intersect) or are parallel.
If two lines are both perpendicular to the same line, they are parallel to each other.

example.q: Look at the capital letter H. Which parts are parallel and which are perpendicular?
steps: The two upright strokes go the same way and never meet, so they are parallel
The middle bar meets each upright stroke at a right angle
example.answer: The two upright strokes are parallel; the middle bar is perpendicular to both of them.

learn.reallife: Ruled lines in your notebook, the steps of a ladder and the opposite edges of a door are all parallel lines.

games.title: Parallel or intersecting?
items: Railway tracks
Opposite edges of a ruler
Lines on a notebook page
Steps of a ladder
The two strokes of the letter X
Open scissor blades
Clock hands at 4 o'clock
Two roads at a crossing

games.title: Line truths
items: Parallel lines will meet if you extend them far enough.
Parallel lines never meet, however far you extend them.
Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.
That is the meaning of perpendicular: they meet at 90°.
Two different lines on a flat page that never meet are parallel.
On a flat surface, lines that never meet are parallel.
The two strokes of the letter V are parallel.
They meet at the bottom point, so they are not parallel.
On a flat page, two lines that are both perpendicular to the same line are parallel to each other.
Both make 90° with the same line, so they go the same way.
Every pair of intersecting lines is perpendicular.
Lines can cross at any angle, like 30° or 120°. Only 90° makes them perpendicular.

quiz.q: Which symbol means 'is parallel to'?
quiz.explain: ∥ (two upright strokes side by side) means parallel. ⊥ means perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the parallel and perpendicular symbols

quiz.q: Two lines are perpendicular. What is the angle between them?
quiz.explain: Perpendicular lines always meet at a right angle, which is 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks perpendicular means a straight line (180°)

quiz.q: Which lines never meet, however far they are extended?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines keep the same distance apart, so they never meet.
quiz.mistake: Thinks perpendicular lines never meet

quiz.q: Riya draws a line l. Then she draws lines m and n, both perpendicular to l. How are m and n related?
options: They are perpendicular to each other
quiz.explain: Both m and n stand at 90° on l, so they point the same way and never meet. They are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two perpendiculars must cross each other

quiz.q: Which is NOT an example of parallel lines?
quiz.explain: Open scissor blades meet at the screw, so they are intersecting, not parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any two straight edges are parallel

quiz.q: Two parallel lines are 3 cm apart at one place. How far apart are they at another place along the lines?
quiz.explain: Parallel lines are the same distance apart everywhere, so it is still 3 cm.
quiz.mistake: Thinks parallel lines come closer far away

quiz.q: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
quiz.explain: Top and bottom sides make one pair, and left and right sides make another pair. That is 2 pairs.
quiz.mistake: Counts each side instead of each pair

quiz.q: How are the two strokes of the capital letter T placed?
quiz.explain: The top bar meets the upright stroke at a right angle, so they are perpendicular.
quiz.mistake: Thinks lines that touch at one end cannot be perpendicular

teach.ask: Gappu is confused: what is the difference between parallel lines and perpendicular lines?
teach.praise: Tweet! Railway tracks are parallel and a notebook corner is perpendicular. Gappu got it!
teach.nudge: Do parallel lines ever meet? And at what angle do perpendicular lines meet?

topics.title: Dot paper: slants, perpendiculars and arrow marks

learn.hook: On dot paper, a line is just a recipe: '3 steps right, 1 step up'. Same recipe — parallel lines!
points: On dot paper we describe a segment by its steps, like '3 right, 1 up'.
Segments with the same slant are parallel: '2 right, 1 up' ∥ '4 right, 2 up' (both steps doubled).
To draw a perpendicular, swap the two step numbers and reverse one direction: '3 right, 1 up' ⊥ '1 left, 3 up'.
Horizontal and vertical segments on dot paper are always perpendicular.
Matching arrow marks (> or >>) on lines in a figure show which lines are parallel.

example.q: Segment PQ goes 4 right and 2 up. Which is parallel to it: '2 right, 1 up' or '1 right, 2 up'?
steps: So '2 right, 1 up' has the same slant

learn.reallife: Floor tiles, ruled notebooks and the lines on a badminton court use parallel and perpendicular lines drawn on a grid.

games.title: Dot paper detective
items: Lines with the same arrow marks are parallel
Arrow marks label parallel lines.
A line going 2 right, 1 up is parallel to one going 1 right, 2 up
Their slants are different.
A line going 1 left, 2 up is perpendicular to one going 2 right, 1 up
Swap the steps and reverse one direction.
A horizontal and a vertical line on dot paper are perpendicular
They meet at 90°.
Arrow marks show the length of a line
They show which lines are parallel.

quiz.q: Which segment is parallel to one going '3 right, 1 up'?
quiz.explain: Doubling both steps keeps the same slant: 6 right, 2 up.
quiz.mistake: Changes only one of the two step numbers

quiz.q: Which segment is perpendicular to one going '3 right, 1 up'?
quiz.explain: Swap 3 and 1, and reverse one direction: 1 left, 3 up.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the numbers but forgets to reverse a direction

quiz.q: Which segment is perpendicular to a horizontal one going '4 right, 0 up'?
quiz.explain: Straight up (vertical) is perpendicular to horizontal.
quiz.mistake: Picks a slanted line

quiz.q: In a figure, two lines are drawn with the same single arrow mark >. What does that tell you?
options: The lines are equal in length
The lines meet at the arrow
quiz.explain: Matching arrow marks are used to show parallel lines.
quiz.mistake: Confuses arrow marks with the right-angle mark

quiz.q: A figure has two lines with single arrows (>) and two lines with double arrows (>>). Which is true?
options: Single-arrow lines are perpendicular to double-arrow lines
Each single-arrow line is parallel to the other single-arrow line
quiz.explain: Only lines with the same number of arrows belong to the same parallel set.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any arrow mark means all the lines are parallel

quiz.q: Segment AB goes 2 right and 5 up. Segment CD is parallel to it and goes 4 right. How many steps up does CD go?
quiz.explain: 4 right is 2 × 2 right, so up must also double: 2 × 5 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 steps instead of doubling

quiz.q: Which pair of segments is parallel?
quiz.explain: 3 right, 6 up is 3 × (1 right, 2 up), so the slant is the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks swapping the numbers keeps the slant

quiz.q: Which steps draw a segment perpendicular to '1 right, 1 up'?
quiz.explain: Swap 1 and 1 (no change) and reverse one direction: 1 right, 1 down.
quiz.mistake: Picks a segment with the same slant

teach.ask: Gappu drew a line '2 right, 1 up' on dot paper. How can Gappu draw a parallel line and a perpendicular line?
teach.praise: Dot-tastic! Gappu drew both lines perfectly.
teach.nudge: What should Gappu do to the steps to make a perpendicular line?

topics.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines by paper folding

learn.hook: Fold a sheet of paper in half three times the same way — open it and you'll find 7 parallel creases!
points: Opposite edges of a rectangular sheet are parallel; adjacent edges are perpendicular.
Folding the left edge onto the right edge makes a crease parallel to those edges and perpendicular to the top and bottom edges.
Folding in half again and again the same way: 1, 3, 7, 15 parallel creases (each fold doubles the parts).
Folding a crease onto itself makes a new crease perpendicular to it.
To check if a crease is parallel to an edge, measure its distance from the edge at both ends — equal distances mean parallel.

example.q: Fold a sheet in half 3 times the same way. How many creases are there when you open it?
steps: The sheet is split into 2 × 2 × 2 = 8 equal strips

learn.reallife: Paper fans, folded maps and origami boats all use parallel and perpendicular creases.

games.title: Rectangle sheet: parallel or perpendicular?
items: Top edge and bottom edge
Top edge and left edge
Left edge and right edge
A crease from folding left edge onto right edge, and the top edge
That crease and the left edge
Bottom edge and right edge

quiz.q: How are the opposite edges of a rectangular sheet of paper related?
quiz.explain: Opposite edges never meet and stay the same distance apart.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up opposite and adjacent edges

quiz.q: How are two adjacent (neighbouring) edges of a rectangular sheet related?
quiz.explain: Adjacent edges meet at a corner of 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every pair of edges is parallel

quiz.q: A sheet is folded in half 2 times the same way. How many creases are there when it is opened?
quiz.explain: 2 folds make 2 × 2 = 4 equal strips, separated by 3 creases.
quiz.mistake: Counts one crease per fold

quiz.q: A sheet is folded in half 4 times the same way. How many parallel creases are there?
quiz.explain: 4 folds make 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16 strips, with 15 creases between them.
quiz.mistake: Counts the strips instead of the creases

quiz.q: The left edge of a sheet is folded onto the right edge. How is the crease related to the top edge?
quiz.explain: The crease runs from top to bottom, meeting the top edge at 90°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every crease is parallel to every edge

quiz.q: You fold a crease onto itself to make a new crease. How is the new crease related to the old one?
quiz.explain: Folding a line onto itself makes two equal angles that together form a straight angle: 90° each.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every new crease is parallel to the old one

quiz.q: How can you check whether a crease is parallel to the bottom edge?
options: Measure its distance from the bottom edge at both ends; equal means parallel
Check that the crease is straight
See whether it touches the edge
Measure the length of the crease
quiz.explain: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart everywhere.
quiz.mistake: Checks the length instead of the distance apart

quiz.q: A sheet is folded once lengthwise and once widthwise. How many creases are there, and how are they related?
quiz.explain: One crease runs along the length and one along the width; they cross at 90°.
quiz.mistake: Assumes all creases are parallel

teach.ask: Gappu folded a paper boat. Show Gappu which creases are parallel and which are perpendicular!
teach.praise: Fold-tastic! Gappu sees lines everywhere in paper now.
teach.nudge: How are the opposite edges of the sheet related, and how are the neighbouring edges related?

learn.hook: One road crossing two parallel roads makes 8 angles — and many of them are hidden twins!
points: A transversal is a line that cuts two (or more) lines at different points. With two lines it makes 8 angles.
Corresponding angles are in the same position at each crossing (think of the letter F).
Alternate interior angles lie between the two lines on opposite sides of the transversal (think of the letter Z).
If the two lines are parallel: corresponding angles are equal, alternate interior angles are equal, and interior angles on the same side add up to 180°.
If corresponding angles (or alternate angles) are equal, then the two lines are parallel.

example.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 70°. Find its corresponding angle, its alternate interior angle and the interior angle on the same side.
steps: Interior angles on the same side add up to 180°: 180° − 70° = 110°

learn.reallife: Zebra crossings, window grills and the lines of a badminton court show transversals cutting parallel lines.

games.title: Parallel lines + transversal
items: Corresponding angles
Alternate interior angles
Vertically opposite angles
Alternate exterior angles
Interior angles on the same side
A linear pair
Exterior angles on the same side

games.title: Angle pair shapes
pairs: Interior angles on the same side

quiz.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is 70°. What is its corresponding angle?
quiz.explain: When lines are parallel, corresponding angles are equal. So it is 70°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks corresponding angles add up to 180°

quiz.q: Lines p and q are parallel. ∠3 = 125° and ∠5 is its alternate interior angle. What is ∠5?
quiz.explain: Alternate interior angles between parallel lines are equal, so ∠5 = 125°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts from 180° as if it were a linear pair

quiz.q: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One interior angle is 75°. What is the interior angle on the same side?
quiz.explain: Interior angles on the same side add up to 180°. 180° − 75° = 105°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks these angles are equal like alternate angles

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines, and a pair of corresponding angles are both 60°. What can you say about the two lines?
quiz.explain: Equal corresponding angles tell us the two lines are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Does not know that equal corresponding angles prove the lines are parallel

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines. A pair of corresponding angles are 80° and 85°. What can you say?
options: The transversal is parallel to them
quiz.explain: If the lines were parallel, the corresponding angles would be equal. 80° ≠ 85°, so the lines are not parallel.
quiz.mistake: Thinks angles that are close are good enough

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines at two different points. How many angles are formed in all?
quiz.explain: Each crossing point makes 4 angles. Two crossing points make 4 + 4 = 8 angles.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the angles at one crossing

quiz.q: A transversal is perpendicular to one of two parallel lines. One interior angle is 90°. What is the interior angle on the same side?
quiz.explain: Same-side interior angles add up to 180°. 180° − 90° = 90°, so the transversal is perpendicular to both lines.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the other angle must be 180°

quiz.q: In the letter Z, the top and bottom strokes are parallel. The angle at the top corner is 40°. What is the angle at the bottom corner?
quiz.explain: The two corner angles of a Z are alternate interior angles between parallel strokes, so they are equal: 40°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the two angles add up to 180°

teach.ask: Gappu sees a road crossing two parallel railway tracks. Which angles are equal, and which add up to 180°?
teach.praise: Fantastic! F and Z angles are twins, and C angles make 180°. Gappu salutes you!
teach.nudge: Which angle pairs are equal when the lines are parallel?

learn.hook: Through a point P outside a line, there is exactly one line parallel to it. Here are three ways to draw it!
points: Task: draw a line through point P parallel to line l.
Sliding method: put a set square's edge on l, hold a ruler against its other edge, slide the set square along the ruler until the edge passes through P, and draw.
Two-perpendiculars method: draw a line through P perpendicular to l, then draw a line at P perpendicular to that line. Both are ⊥ to the same line, so it is ∥ l.
Corresponding-angle method: draw a transversal through P cutting l, then copy the same angle at P in the corresponding position.
Illusions: slanted lines crossing two parallel lines can make them look bent — always check with a ruler.

example.q: A transversal through P makes 60° with line l. How do you draw the parallel line through P?
steps: At P, on the same side and in the same position, draw an angle of 60°
Equal corresponding angles mean the lines are parallel

learn.reallife: Carpenters and tailors use set squares and rulers in exactly this sliding way to draw parallel lines on wood and cloth.

games.title: Two-perpendiculars method
items: Draw line l and mark point P
Draw a line through P perpendicular to l
At P, draw a line perpendicular to this new line
The last line is parallel to l

games.title: Drawing truths
items: Two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel
That is why the two-perpendiculars method works.
In the angle-copying method, the angle at P must equal the angle at l
Equal corresponding angles make the lines parallel.
If parallel lines look bent in a picture, they cannot be parallel
It can be an illusion; measure to check.
Sliding a set square along a ruler keeps its edge pointing the same way
So each new position of the edge is parallel to the first.
Any line through P is parallel to l
Only one line through P is parallel to l.

quiz.q: In the two-perpendiculars method, why is the final line parallel to l?
options: Both lines are the same length
Both lines are drawn with a ruler
Both lines are perpendicular to the same line
quiz.explain: Two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel to each other.
quiz.mistake: Gives a reason that does not involve angles

quiz.q: A transversal through P makes 65° with line l. What angle must be drawn at P, in the corresponding position, to get a parallel line?
quiz.explain: Corresponding angles must be equal for the lines to be parallel.
quiz.mistake: Uses the linear-pair angle instead of the equal angle

quiz.q: When you slide a set square along a ruler, what stays the same?
quiz.explain: The set square only slides, it does not turn, so each edge keeps its direction.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the distance stays the same instead of the direction

quiz.q: How many different lines can be drawn through point P (not on l) parallel to l?
quiz.explain: There is exactly one line through P parallel to l.
quiz.mistake: Thinks many parallels can pass through one point

quiz.q: Riya drew a transversal through P. The angle at l was 70°, and she drew 110° at P in the corresponding position. Is her line parallel to l?
options: No — corresponding angles must be equal
quiz.explain: For corresponding angles, equal means parallel. 70° and 110° are not equal.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the corresponding-angle rule with the interior-angle rule

quiz.q: In a picture, two lines look curved because slanted lines cross them. How can you check whether they are parallel?
options: Measure the gap between them at several places
quiz.explain: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart, so equal gaps everywhere means parallel.
quiz.mistake: Trusts the look of the picture

quiz.q: Which tools does the sliding method use?
options: A ruler and a set square
quiz.explain: The set square slides along a ruler held still.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up this method with another construction

quiz.q: What is the first step in the corresponding-angle method?
options: Draw a circle with centre P
Draw a transversal through P that cuts l
quiz.explain: We need a transversal to have an angle at l that we can copy at P.
quiz.mistake: Starts measuring before there is an angle to measure

teach.ask: Gappu needs a line through P parallel to l, but has only a ruler and a set square. Teach Gappu!
teach.praise: Perfect! Gappu's line is exactly parallel.
teach.nudge: What should Gappu keep still, and what should Gappu slide?

topics.title: Finding unknown angles with parallel lines

learn.hook: One angle given, a whole figure solved — angle facts work like a chain of dominoes!
points: Use one fact at a time: vertically opposite angles are equal, a linear pair adds to 180°.
With parallel lines: corresponding angles are equal, alternate angles are equal, interior angles on the same side add to 180°.
Lines are parallel only if corresponding (or alternate) angles are equal, or same-side interior angles add to 180°.
Bent-line trick: if l ∥ m and a path bends at X between them, draw a line through X parallel to l. The angle at X = sum of the two alternate angles.
Two angles in a linear pair with one 3 times the other: 4 equal parts make 180°, so 45° and 135°.

example.q: l ∥ m. A path goes from l to X to m. The angle with l is 40° and the angle with m is 30°. Find the angle at X.
steps: Draw a line through X parallel to l (and m)
Top part of ∠X = 40° (alternate to the angle at l)
Bottom part of ∠X = 30° (alternate to the angle at m)

learn.reallife: Engineers check that railway tracks and bridge beams are parallel by measuring such angles.

items.q: Bent line: 35° and 45°, angle at X
Linear partner of a 60° corresponding angle

games.title: Parallel or not?
items: Corresponding angles 70° and 70°
Alternate angles 55° and 65°
Same-side interior angles 100° and 80°
Same-side interior angles 90° and 95°
Alternate angles 120° and 120°
Corresponding angles 45° and 54°

quiz.q: l ∥ m. An angle at l is 65°. Its corresponding angle is at m. What is the angle forming a linear pair with that corresponding angle?
quiz.explain: Corresponding angle = 65°. Its linear-pair partner = 180° − 65° = 115°.
quiz.mistake: Stops after the first step

quiz.q: l ∥ m. An interior angle at l is 118°. What is the interior angle on the same side at m?
quiz.explain: Same-side interior angles add to 180°: 180° − 118° = 62°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks same-side interior angles are equal

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines making alternate angles of 72° and 78°. Are the lines parallel?
quiz.explain: For parallel lines, alternate angles must be equal. 72° ≠ 78°.
quiz.mistake: Thinks angles that are close enough count as equal

quiz.q: A transversal cuts two lines making same-side interior angles of 110° and 70°. Are the lines parallel?
options: No, because they are not equal
quiz.explain: Same-side interior angles adding to 180° shows the lines are parallel.
quiz.mistake: Expects same-side interior angles to be equal

quiz.q: l ∥ m. A path bends at X between them. It makes 40° with l and 30° with m (alternate positions). What is the angle at X?
quiz.explain: Draw a line through X parallel to l. The angle at X splits into 40° and 30°: total 70°.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the two angles

quiz.q: l ∥ m. A bent path has angle 95° at X. One part (alternate to the angle at l) is 55°. What angle does the path make with m?
quiz.explain: ∠X = angle with l + angle with m, so 95° − 55° = 40°.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: The rungs of a ladder are parallel. A side rail makes 75° with one rung. What angle does it make with the next rung in the same position?
quiz.explain: The rail is a transversal and the angles are corresponding, so they are equal.
quiz.mistake: Uses 180° − 75° for corresponding angles

quiz.q: Two angles form a linear pair and one is 3 times the other. What is the larger angle?
quiz.explain: Together they make 4 equal parts = 180°, so one part is 45° and the larger is 3 × 45° = 135°.
quiz.mistake: Divides 180° by 3 instead of 4

teach.ask: Gappu sees l ∥ m with a zig-zag path between them. How can Gappu find the angle at the bend?
teach.praise: Zig-zag solved! Gappu adds the two alternate angles.
teach.nudge: What extra line could Gappu draw through the bend?
